title: How a forest is born (a 120-year timelapse)
_shots: M = the master timelapse (every beat from hook to why, contiguous, one continuous camera move); R = the rewind (ask + loop) that runs the clock back to year 0 so the last frame equals frame 0. Frame counts are filled in from timeline.json by the scene (--shot M --end 0 means 'all'); the numbers below are copied from tts.py output.

years._comment: year of the timelapse at the start and end of each beat; the scene (scene_forest.py) and the overlay (beats.js) both interpolate linearly inside a beat so the counter matches the footage. ask/loop rewind to 0 with an ease (see yearAt in both).

lines: Leave bare dirt alone, and it grows a forest. By itself.
Year one: weeds. Their seeds ride the wind, and all they need is sun.
Year five: grasses take over. Dead leaves rot into richer soil.
Year fifteen: birds drop berry seeds. Shrubs. The first shade.
Year thirty: birch and pine race up for the light. But they can't grow in shade. Not even their own.
Year one hundred: oaks and maples rise underneath them, and take over. The forest is born.
Each stage changes the ground, kills the stage before it, and makes room for the next. That's succession.
Every empty lot is on this clock. What's growing in the cracks near you?
